subject: Unexpected invoice spike — request for token attribution and sample session breakdown
messages:
From: Oliver Price <oliver.price@syncnova.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@syncnova.com, syncnova-billing@syncnova.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice IN-0425 — sudden usage spike, need attribution

Hi Hannah,

We received invoice IN-0425 this morning and are seeing a ~4.6x jump in billed tokens for the period 2027-03-15 — 2027-04-14 compared to prior month. I've attached the usage export our team pulled and the invoice PDF.

Can you provide: 
- A short explanation for what is being counted as tokens here (streaming vs batch vs embed-replay attribution).
- A sample of session-level lines that show the counts attributed to SyncNova (we're especially interested in any sessions starting with "sn-"; sample id sn-78934 is one we found).
- Confirmation whether any replays/ingests or background batch jobs might have been charged to our account.

We need this for our procurement review. If there's an obvious over-bill, we will request a credit. Please let us know estimated turnaround — procurement is hoping for a response within 72 hours.

Attached: usage_export_202704.csv (csv), invoice_IN-0425.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Price
Head of Platform Operations
SyncNova, Inc.
oliver.price@syncnova.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Price <oliver.price@syncnova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice IN-0425 — sudden usage spike, need attribution

Hi Oliver — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the export.

Ben and Priyom, looping you both in to validate token attribution and check whether any ingest/replay jobs were incorrectly credited to SyncNova. Ben — can you confirm whether streaming vs non-streaming paths (or embedding replays) could produce a 4x billing delta in a single month?

Oliver — we'll aim to get a preliminary assessment within 48 hours. To speed things up, could you confirm:
- Whether the sample session id sn-78934 you mentioned corresponds to a customer-facing session or an async ingest job.
- Any API call ids (X-Request-Id) around 2027-04-06 02:00–04:00 UTC if you have them.

Ben/Priyom — if you need a deeper export, I can request extended logs from infra; just confirm what format you want (CSV with call ids / gzipped NDJSON).

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Oliver Price <oliver.price@syncnova.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice IN-0425 — sudden usage spike, need attribution

Hi Oliver — I pulled a quick sample against the usage export you sent. Attaching an excerpt (sample_lines_sn-78934.csv) with the relevant rows. Some quick notes from the prelim review:

- Attribution nuance: our metering attributes tokens to the request context id that triggered generation. If a downstream background job (e.g., an embedding replay or a batch reindex) re-requests a model using the original session prefix, that job may be recorded under a different request id but still associated with your project, which can look like duplicated session traffic.

- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming responses are metered per token the same as non-streaming, but streaming pipelines can produce extra tokens if the client resends partial ranges or reconnects mid-stream. We saw a cluster of reconnects on 2027-04-06 02:45–03:05 UTC in the sample.

- Possible root causes for a 4x spike (prelim): 1) bulk reindex/replay job ran (attributed to your project), 2) a client-side loop that resubmitted requests on error, 3) a duplicate ingestion pipeline misconfigured during a deploy.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Oliver — confirm whether you ran any scheduled batch jobs in early April (reindex, embed-replay, or large reingest).
2) If not, provide a couple of X-Request-Id values from the rows you care about and we'll pull the full call traces for those ids.
3) We'll produce a 72-hour timeline and a proposed remediation/credit if we confirm misattribution.

I've attached sample_lines_sn-78934.csv (includes request_id, timestamp, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, attribution_key). If you can point to 2–3 request ids, we can escalate to infra for trace captures.

Ben Carter
Billing & Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference
Attached: sample_lines_sn-78934.csv

From: Oliver Price <oliver.price@syncnova.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@syncnova.com, syncnova-billing@syncnova.com
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice IN-0425 — sudden usage spike, need attribution

Thanks, Ben — appreciate the quick review.

We confirmed that sn-78934 is a customer-facing conversational session; however, we do have a nightly embedding replay job (job id er-20270406) that ran on 2027-04-06 02:47 UTC. The replay job's logs show request ids xreq-0a1b2c3d and xreq-0a1b2c3e for the chunked replays.

We did not intentionally run duplicate jobs; the replay was part of a scheduled reindex. Given your notes about attribution, it sounds like these replays may have been billed back to our production sessions rather than the ingest job.

Request: if you confirm misattribution after trace analysis, we'd ask for a billing credit equal to the amount billed for the two replay request ids (estimate included in the attached invoice excerpt). Procurement would like a resolution (credit or adjustment) within 7 business days so we can close our PO hold.

Next steps per your email look good — we'll send any additional request ids if infra finds more. For urgency, do you need us to open a formal support ticket or is this handled under your billing ops queue?

Oliver
Oliver Price
Head of Platform Operations
SyncNova, Inc.
Attached: invoice_excerpt_for_credit.png
